links.outcome: Correct diagnostic rate and referral rate with versus without EyeFM copilot in RCT
links.effect: Correct diagnostic rate 92.2% vs 75.4% (P<0.001); referral rate 92.2% vs 80.5% (P<0.001); higher patient compliance with self-management (70.1% vs 49.1%) and referral (33.7% vs 20.2%).
links.quote: The primary endpoint indicated that ophthalmologists with EyeFM copilot achieved higher correct diagnostic rate (92.2% versus 75.4%, P < 0.001) and referral rate (92.2% versus 80.5%, P < 0.001).

links.outcome: Ophthalmologist diagnostic performance with versus without AI copilot in intended deployment mode
links.effect: Ophthalmologists with EyeFM copilot had higher correct diagnostic rate (92.2% vs 75.4%, P<0.001) than standard care; overreliance not reported in the abstract.
links.quote: The primary endpoint indicated that ophthalmologists with EyeFM copilot achieved higher correct diagnostic rate (92.2% versus 75.4%, P < 0.001) and referral rate (92.2% versus 80.5%, P < 0.001).

screen.reason: The study is a randomized controlled trial evaluating the deployment of a vision-language foundation model as a copilot for ophthalmologists in real clinical practice compared to standard care.

primary.practice: AI copilot assistance for clinical decision-making
